title: Microshard allocator for smooth FlashAttention v2→v3 transition
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: During mixed-traffic rollouts that enable FlashAttention v3 alongside v2, we've observed transient latency and OOM spikes caused by coarse-grained kernel handoffs and buffer reallocation at prefill→decode boundaries. This ticket implements a microshard allocator and staged handoff protocol to smooth memory transitions and reduce decode jitter when kernels switch between v2 and v3 variants. The allocator splits large workspace requests into smaller 'microshards' that can be migrated incrementally, letting the runtime interleave warmup and eviction with lower tail-latency impact. Goals: reduce 95th/99th latency delta between v2-only and v2/v3-mixed traffic by >=30%, reduce spike OOM incidents on 80/160-token workloads, and provide observability hooks for shard-level allocation events.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator integrates with kernel scheduler and can allocate/migrate microshards at runtime
End-to-end e2e canary shows <=30% regression reduction in 95th latency compared to current mixed rollouts
No increase in steady-state memory usage beyond 5% for typical 8k/16k models
Telemetry emits shard_migration_start, shard_migration_end, shard_eviction events and they appear in Console traces
Unit and integration tests cover cross-precision (fp16/quan) and multi-GPU shards
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Raman: Added initial ticket after postmortem review of canary on 2025-02-16. Observed repeated prefills failing when v3 kernels activated concurrently with cold KV cache. Proposed microshard approach to avoid monolithic reallocations.

2025-02-19 - Marco Li: Spike implementation started. Built allocator prototype that slices workspace into fixed 128KB microshards. Early local tests show decode tail latency smoothing on small batch sizes but higher fragmentation overhead — need reclamation policy.

2025-02-20 - Ryan Chen (review): Concern about per-request overhead. Suggests batching shard ops for requests sharing the same model and placement to amortize locking. Also recommended adding a lightweight fast-path for requests that fully fit existing contiguous workspace.

2025-02-21 - Marco Li: Implemented batched shard ops and fast-path check. Benchmarks on p4d show 22% reduction in 95th for 128-token prefill→decode compared to baseline mixed rollout. Fragmentation metric still high for adversarial small requests pattern.
2025-02-22 - Design review (Sofia Kim): UX note - Console should surface shard-level heatmaps and a per-model fragmentation score. Added story for Console integration in a follow-up ticket.
2025-02-24 - Marco Li: Integrated telemetry hooks for shard_migration_start/end + reason tag (handshake, eviction, compaction). Instrumented runtime traces with sampling to avoid high cardinality.

2025-02-25 - QA (Priya Nair): Created integration tests that simulate simultaneous v2/v3 kernel activation storms. Found a race where two threads attempt to migrate overlapping shards leading to double-free in debug build. Added shard migration lock and idempotency guard. Need to run full CI and perf run on staging before marking Done.

Next steps: schedule staging perf run with 48-hour traffic replay (2025-03-01), open follow-up ENG for Console heatmap story, and prepare a canary rollout plan tied to shard-migration telemetry thresholds.
